cards.canonical_statement: Given an actual total derivative A of a scalar f on ℝⁿ at x, a proposed ith coordinate partial value c is valid exactly when c=A(eᵢ). The coordinate slice is evaluated at xᵢ.
cards.proof_strategy: Use the known total derivative to obtain an actual derivative of the coordinate slice.
sketch_steps: Use the known total derivative to obtain an actual derivative of the coordinate slice.
The update curve passes through x at parameter xᵢ with velocity eᵢ.
Uniqueness forces any proposed coordinate partial c to equal A(eᵢ).
Conversely, that equality identifies c with the already established derivative.

cards.canonical_statement: For arbitrary nonempty coordinate dimensions m,n, there exists f:ℝᵐ→ℝⁿ that is not differentiable at the origin while every entry of Lean’s totalized Jacobian there is zero. Therefore a zero Jacobian expression without a differentiability premise is not evidence of an actual zero derivative.
cards.proof_strategy: Construct every output coordinate as the absolute value of one chosen input coordinate.
sketch_steps: Construct every output coordinate as the absolute value of one chosen input coordinate.
If the map were differentiable, restricting to that coordinate line and projecting to an output would make absolute value differentiable at zero.
This contradicts nondifferentiability of absolute value at zero.
Lean totalizes fderiv to zero in this case, and its standard matrix has all entries zero.

by
  let f : (Fin m → ℝ) → (Fin n → ℝ) := fun x _ => |x i|
  have hn : ¬DifferentiableAt ℝ f 0 := by
    intro h
    have hs : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun t : ℝ => f (Pi.single i t) j) 0 := by
      have hp : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun x => f x j) (Pi.single i (0 : ℝ)) := by
        simpa using (differentiableAt_pi.mp h) j

    apply not_differentiableAt_abs_zero
    simpa [f] using hs
  refine ⟨f,hn,?_⟩
  intro r c
  simp [fderiv_zero_of_not_differentiableAt hn]

cards.canonical_statement: For differentiable f:ℝᵐ→ℝⁿ at c(t) and a curve c with velocity u at t, the composite curve s↦f(c(s)) has velocity Jf(c(t))u. The dimensions and matrix multiplication order are explicit.
sketch_steps: Construct the composite curve explicitly.
Apply the curve chain rule using the actual derivative at c(t).
Convert the derivative map into its standard-coordinate Jacobian.
Its application to u is exactly matrix-vector multiplication Jf(c(t))u.

cards.canonical_statement: For all nonempty coordinate dimensions m,n and nonzero real c, there exists a Lebesgue-integrable f on ℝᵐ×ℝⁿ whose entire section at x=0 equals c and is not integrable. Fubini ensures integrable sections almost everywhere, not at every point.
cards.proof_strategy: Set f(x,y)=c when x=0 and zero otherwise.
sketch_steps: Set f(x,y)=c when x=0 and zero otherwise.
The exceptional hyperplane has product measure zero, so f is almost everywhere zero and integrable.
Its section at x=0 is the nonzero constant c.
Lebesgue measure of positive-dimensional ℝⁿ is infinite, hence that constant section is not integrable.
